teaser.text: The Home Depot is a retailer and distributor of products, equipment, and services for building, repairing, maintaining, and furnishing property. It makes money when the value of those goods and services exceeds the cost of buying, moving, staffing, and supporting them.

stock.title: Home Depot stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Home Depot's forecast weighs bear, base and bull scenarios, then tests the cash generation and valuation behind the shares.
stock.opening: Home Depot's weighted forecast reaches $381.13 by October 2029, including dividends. It hinges on Home Depot's organic Pro growth, reliable fulfillment and cash returns from SRS and GMS.
stock.closing: The full memo also covers Home Depot's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could Home Depot's shares go?

paragraphs.text: The weighted price is $308.65 in October 2027 and $340.36 in October 2028, including dividends. It reaches $381.13 in October 2029, a 41% total return from today’s price. The October 2029 range runs from $250.71 in the bear case to $530.49 in the bull case.
The bear case receives 28%. The base case receives the highest probability, at 52%. The bull case receives 20%.

blocks.heading: What could move Home Depot's stock forecast?

paragraphs.text: The bear case uses lower revenue, beginning at $168,000 million and $170,000 million in the first two periods. It reaches $174,000 million in the final period, with margins of 12.2%, 12.3% and 12.5%. The bull case reaches $177,000 million, $186,000 million and $196,000 million, while margins recover to the historical average by 2029. The evidence supports both caution and upside: transactions fell 1.0%, but online comparable sales grew 11% and SRS cross-selling reached an annualized $400 million pace.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Home Depot really make?

paragraphs.text: After **$3,679 million** of capital spending, free cash flow was **$12,646 million**. After **$522 million** of stock-based pay, the analytical “real free cash flow” was **$12,124 million**. Net acquisition payments were **$5,410 million**, while dividends were **$9,152 million**. Cash generation was therefore substantial, but the year’s post-investment cash did not cover both acquisitions and distributions.

dividend.title: Home Depot dividend: cash coverage and outlook
dividend.meta_description: Home Depot's dividend is supported by substantial free cash flow, but acquisitions, debt and demand shape its outlook.
dividend.opening: Home Depot’s forecast dividend is $9.32 per share in 2027, rising to $9.70 by 2029. Its fiscal 2025 free cash flow was $12,646 million against $9,152 million of dividends, but acquisitions meant post-investment cash did not cover both acquisitions and distributions.
dividend.closing: The full memo also explains Home Depot’s business, its rivals, its management and its risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Home Depot pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: The base dividend is $9.32 per share in 2027, rising to $9.51 and $9.70. The bear case holds it at $9.32, while the bull case reaches $9.88 and $10.47. The base path fits a long record of uninterrupted quarterly payments, but also recognizes that the latest increase was only 1.3% and free cash flow fell 22.5%.

blocks.heading: What could change Home Depot's dividend?

paragraphs.text: The first test is FY2026 execution against management’s sales growth, comparable-sales and operating-margin guidance. Transactions recovering alongside average tickets would move the forecast toward the base or bull cases; another period of falling transactions would support the bear case.

Capital allocation is the next test. Repurchases resuming by the expected date would support the base case, while larger purchases would require stronger cash generation after investment, dividends and debt reduction. Failure to reduce leverage would keep the share count and multiple closer to the bear case.

earnings.title: Home Depot earnings: guidance and what to watch
earnings.meta_description: Home Depot reports on November 17, 2026; see its guidance, recent results and what to watch next.
earnings.opening: Home Depot's next results are expected on November 17, 2026. The one thing to watch is whether more sales reflect more projects, not just larger tickets.
earnings.closing: The full memo also explains Home Depot's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: What has Home Depot guided for fiscal 2026?

paragraphs.text: Home Depot expects fiscal 2026 to be a year of modest growth while larger projects wait for easier financing.

Management kept its annual gross-margin and operating-margin outlook unchanged. Higher fuel, energy and product costs are expected to absorb the refund’s benefit over the year, so the second-quarter boost does not by itself change the underlying profit promise.

blocks.heading: Did Home Depot keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: The annual incentive paid 95% of target, while the completed three-year performance-share award paid 70.1%. On November 18, 2025, Decker acknowledged that quarterly results missed expectations and management lowered its outlook. Fiscal 2025 adjusted earnings per share fell 3.6%, but that was better than the revised forecast of an approximately 5% decline. Management met the reduced expectation, while still delivering lower earnings.

blocks.heading: What do Home Depot's last eight quarters show?

paragraphs.text: The latest quarter showed better sales, but its profit increase depended partly on a tariff refund while customer transactions kept falling.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in Home Depot's next results?

paragraphs.text: Home Depot reports third-quarter results on November 17, 2026. Investors should separate acquired revenue, price increases and comparable growth, then examine customer transactions, average purchase size and large-project demand. More sales dollars do not necessarily mean that more projects took place.
